name: Layouts
what: Encyclopedia of every way a page can divide its room, with IDs combining column count and division name, drawn at three widths.
parts: Tree view grouped by column count
features: Point at screenshot and name the ID
Click tags to see similar layouts
See CSS grid and flex recipes
Find real websites using each layout

demos.shows: Twelve layouts drawn at three widths, organized by column count

blurb: Every layout named, defined and drawn at three widths.

stage.should_cap: Layout drawings are scaled/zoomed, no full-bleed spreading

name: Browse
what: Every layout on the site displayed as pictures in three tiers (global, sections, components) with approve and improve verdict buttons.

demos.shows: Three walls of layout pictures with tier selector and verdict marks
Single layout at three widths with decisions and verdict interface

gaps: Cannot add or delete items from UI
Verdict buttons only work on dev server
Does not show interactivity of layouts
blurb: Every layout on the site in three tiers, approve or improve each.

stage.should_cap: Card wall stretches but no individual card spreads past measure

name: Practice
what: Three full-page layouts (workbench, reader, catalog) built at 3440 and responsive to 400, filled with real site content and showing design decisions.
parts: Workbench page with panel and tile grid
Reader page with article and margin
Catalog page with hero, card wall, footer
features: See responsive behavior at actual width

demos.shows: Three-column layout with panel on left, tiles on right at 3440
Article reading layout with wide margin at 3440
Hero, card wall, and footer layout at 3440

gaps: Only shown at one primary viewport width at a time
Responsive behavior to other widths not demonstrated
Edge cases and error states not shown
blurb: Three layouts built big, filled with site content and decisions.

stage.should_cap: These pages are designed for 3440 and spread to that width intentionally

name: Shell
what: A resizable sidebar with tree navigation and viewport beside it showing eight homepage designs, each changing one design decision from its parent.

demos.shows: Base homepage with seven variations accessible via tree, viewport responds to sidebar width

gaps: Only one design visible at a time
Cannot compare two designs side-by-side
No export or save functionality
Desktop-only interaction pattern
blurb: Resizable sidebar and tree of homepage designs varying one change at a time.

stage.should_cap: Fills viewport edge-to-edge for sidebar and design view

name: Labs
what: Six shape experiments moved from /imagine/ with demonstrations: app shells, click behavior, horizontal band, blog at 3440, magazine, and deck layouts.
parts: Shells lab with app chrome variants
Decks lab for deck with regions
features: Understand what earned each an id

demos.shows: Ten app shell variations demonstrating different chrome approaches
Click behavior demonstrations showing screen changes

gaps: Limited responsive demonstrations
Not all experiments fully interactive
Research process explanation missing
Comparison between experiments not provided
blurb: Six shape experiments moved from /imagine/, arrangements earning ids.

stage.should_cap: Experiments use full width, may spread at 3440

name: Tags
what: Navigation system where clicking any layout tag (technique, word, trait) shows every layout that carries it.

demos.shows: Tag chip row and word definitions with example layouts

gaps: Does not show full layout pages with CSS
Need to click through to see details
Real sites data only shown if corpus populated
No multi-tag filtering
blurb: Click any tag to see every layout that carries it.

stage.should_cap: Tag row and layout wall stay within measure

name: Docs
what: Three technical reference documents defining the layout standard: naming rules, wire drawing specification, and settlement record.
gaps: No interactive demonstrations
No visual examples of naming or wires in docs
Heavy on reference, light on tutorial
Cannot experiment with naming rules
blurb: Naming rules, wire spec, and settlement record for the standard.
